meta: Dramas like Another Miss Oh: Park Hae Young's writing, coincidence as plot, and the shows that treat their heroine better.
standfirst: Two women with the same name, a man who sees the future in fragments, and a comedy that keeps turning into a melodrama. An 8.1 aggregate against a 6.46 written-review average and 4.54 rewatch is the widest negative gap on this shelf, and it is earned twice over. Seo Hyun Jin is extraordinary and the couple is the most physically convincing pairing in this catalog. The premise is also indefensible: the male lead detonates a wedding for his own reasons and the script spends the back half quietly reducing what he is responsible for. Loving the craft and hating the show are both correct positions here.

picks.why: Same writer, and this is the one she is remembered for. Park Hae Young again on people who are humiliated at work and worse at home, with the same ear for dialogue that sounds overheard rather than written. Difference: pace 1, romance 1 and comfort 4, and it is fundamentally decent to everybody in it, which is the exact repair Another Miss Oh needs. Park Hae Young wrote this two years before My Mister, which is why the later show reads as the correction: same eye for a woman being ground down, none of the ugliness played as romance.

Her other great one, and the same interest in people who cannot ask for what they want. Same writer, same long silences, same conviction that a small life deserves sixteen hours. Difference: pace 1 and romance 2, with almost no plot at all, so the farce and the coincidence engine here are replaced by weather and commuting.

Shared cast, and the same reliance on near-misses. Same structure of a plot that only moves because people fail to say the obvious thing, same braid of comedy and grief. Difference: an 8.75 written-review average against 6.46 here, and it is kind to everybody, so the mean streak is gone.

Shared cast, and a heroine the show actually likes. Same small-world comedy melodrama with a large gossiping ensemble and a thriller humming underneath. Difference: comfort 5 and it is built on giving its lead dignity, which is precisely the axis on which Another Miss Oh fails.

The adult romance conducted in complete sentences. Same generation, same money problems, same interest in what two people owe each other. Difference: it is dry and calm with no makjang at all, so nobody is deceived, nobody is humiliated, and the plot moves because people decide things.

Shared cast, and comedy that likes its characters. Same 2016 comic register and the same pleasure of watching somebody be embarrassing and be loved anyway. Difference: comfort 5, heavy 1 and a campus setting, so the adult melodrama and the premonition device have no place in it.

against.title: Fight for My Way
against.why: Paired constantly as the other late-twenties comedy of the same era, and the difference is respect. Fight for My Way likes its heroine and lets her win arguments. Another Miss Oh spends eighteen episodes on a woman apologising for existing, and if that is what you liked, this will not scratch it.

against.title: Oh My Ghost
against.why: Recommended for the comedy-melodrama blend and the possession-adjacent gimmick. It has a serial killer, a chef and a much broader comic engine, and it never sits in the discomfort. The unease is half of what makes Another Miss Oh distinctive.

against.title: Temperature of Love
against.why: The default adult romance from the same window, and it is inert. Two people talk about their feelings for thirty half-hours with no engine at all. Another Miss Oh is badly behaved but never boring, and losing the plot machinery loses the reason to stay.
